summary: Task 7 correctly migrates the editor page from three flat trigger refs to a triggers: FunnelTrigger[] ref, rewrites persist() with a per-element sanitizer, makes triggerReady() per-element, gates the debounced autosave on triggers.every(triggerReady), and mounts FunnelTriggersPanel via v-model:triggers. The re-entrancy guard is robust: applyResponse() always reassigns triggers.value to a fresh array identity so the deep watch always fires and consumes the one pending applyingResponse flag, and sequential real edits each persist (verified empirically). All acceptance criteria are met, no regressions found, 47 tests pass, and no stale refs/imports remain.

suggestions.suggestion: Theoretical (not reachable in practice) coalescing race in the re-entrancy guard: if applyResponse() and a user edit were ever batched into a single deep-watch flush, that one watch callback would see applyingResponse===true, consume it, and return — silently dropping the user edit. This cannot occur in the current code because applyResponse() is always called after an await (network settle), and Vue flushes watchers on the following microtask, so a user DOM event cannot interleave into that exact tick. If a future refactor ever calls applyResponse() synchronously alongside a user mutation, this guard would need a more precise signal (e.g. comparing the applied array identity) instead of a one-shot boolean. Worth a one-line note on the guard but not a change today.
suggestions.benefit: Documents a latent assumption so a future synchronous applyResponse() call site does not silently regress autosave.

suggestions.suggestion: sanitizeTrigger() carries entryStepId through as-is for ALL trigger types (entryStepId: tr.entryStepId ?? null), relying on the panel to only ever set it for event triggers. This is correct today (on_start/keyword/etc. never get an entry picker, so their entryStepId stays null) and the backend is the final validator per Decision 10, but defensively forcing entryStepId to null for non-event types in the sanitizer would make the page robust against any future panel change that accidentally leaves a stale entryStepId on a non-event trigger.
suggestions.benefit: Defense-in-depth: the page's PATCH payload would honor Decision 10 (mid-entry is event-only) independent of the panel's behavior.
